text:
maria: Heads-up — after landing the slab-slicing change + new FP8 scaling heuristic I'm seeing ~2x all-reduce tail latency on TP x4 with 32B sequences. KV cache hit rate also dropped ~12% for short prompts. Any ideas?

josh: Ugh. saw something similar on my perf branch last week but chalked it up to NCCL scheduling. Do you have a profile?

maria: Pasted a short perf snapshot from perf-bot: 
```
GPU0 compute  85ms
GPU0 allreduce  120ms (tail spikes to 260ms)
GPU1 compute  80ms
GPU1 allreduce  115ms
KV cache lookup  miss rate 0.18 -> 0.30 (post-change)
Batching: avg batch size 3.2 -> 2.1 (more micro-batches)
```

li: Two things that jump out: (1) batching shrinkage -> smaller allreduce payloads + higher relative overhead; (2) FP8 quant path might change kernel placement and buffer alignment, causing suboptimal NCCL buffer sizes.

dana: Also check whether slab-slicing moved tensors off 256B alignment, NCCL performs worse with non-contiguous reductions. Can you dump dtypes/strides for the KV tensors?

maria: Dump: 
```
KV.keys dtype=int8 (quantized), shape=(4, seq_len, head_dim) stride=(head_dim,1,1)
KV.values dtype=fp8_e4m3, shape=(4, seq_len, head_dim) stride=(head_dim,1,1)
```

josh: fp8_e4m3 on KV.values — that might be the culprit. We've seen reduced alignment when mixing INT8 keys + FP8 values. Try forcing FP32 for KV.values as an experiment (cheap to patch).

li: Another quick check: set NCCL_ALGO to ring and NCCL_MIN_NRINGS=1, see if tail goes away. If ring gives better tail, it's comm scheduling.

maria: I ran two quick experiments: (A) fallback KV.values -> fp32: allreduce tail back to normal, KV hit rate recovered. (B) keep fp8 but set NCCL_ALGO=ring: tail improves by ~30% but KV miss still high.

maria: Relevant log snippet after (A):
```
[run A] allreduce p99 130ms -> 68ms
[run A] KV miss 0.30 -> 0.19
```

dana: That strongly points to quant codec causing different packing/strides which increases packing/unpacking overhead and reduces effective cacheability of prefixes. Maybe our slab-slicer is slicing inside the quant block instead of before quantization.

josh: Agreed. Two actionable items: (1) ensure slab-slicing happens pre-quant (so quant kernels see full contiguous buffers); (2) add a fallback kernel path that keeps KV.values in fp32 for small seqs or when TP>1 + quant enabled.

li: Also update batching heuristic: if avg batch size falls below 2.5 due to slicing, prefer to coalesce micro-batches for the allreduce path. That reduces allreduce latency amortization.

maria: Created a quick canary: revert quant-op ordering so we quantize after slicing + add coalesce window (50ms). Running now.

perf-bot: Canary run 1 finished. Summary:
- allreduce p99 down 45%
- avg batch size up from 2.1 -> 3.6
- KV miss 0.30 -> 0.20

maria: Good signal. Two follow-ups: (1) engage runtime to add unit test that validates contiguous strides post-slicing; (2) add telemetry that emits "quant-packing-alignment" tag if buffer stride != expected.

dana: I'll own the unit test + telemetry. josh/li can you review the kernel fallback?

josh: On it. I'll sketch a fallback that triggers when TP>1 and seq_len>=32 and quant path active. Keep it cheap.

li: I'll file a perf task to tune batching heuristics and add an experiment to test NCCL ring vs tree across different payload sizes.

maria: Thanks all. TL;DR: root cause appears to be ordering of slab-slicing vs quant + buffer alignment; quick canary shows big improvement. We'll roll to staging after unit tests and a small kernel fallback. :thumbsup:

maria: tagging @eng-runtime for visibility and @perf-bench when we push the benchmark changes.
